impact_map: GL4SS planner prompt assembly and deterministic still/cinematic compiler
portable skill instructions, references, templates, evals, and host metadata
place-time grounding, optic support, habitation, precision, scenario, comparison, and traversal behavior
render authority and truthful tool-state reporting

invariants.statement: Drop-ins target one exact GL4SS commit and apply in planner-then-renderer order.
The patches add no model call, provider, dependency, storage layer, UI, or public TypeScript field.
The view carries only the temporal, geographic, habitation, and scenario precision earned by input and sources.
Every viewpoint has honest physical support, safe standoff, or an explicit virtual aperture.
One authorized render is distinct from text-only work; multi-render routes state count before host authority.
Dispatch, returned output, failed render, prompt-only, and source-unavailable remain distinct states.
The twelve portable files remain byte-identical between Codex portable content and Claude distribution.
Every delivered file is checksummed; the Claude ZIP has one safe root; local links resolve; private host paths are absent.
Private-handoff claims remain bounded from live-host, provider, rendered-quality, public-license, and accessibility-conformance claims.

risks.statement: When the drop-ins are applied to the wrong GL4SS bytes or exceed their bounded seams, the application can fail or silently change public behavior outside the proposal.
When a broad date or famous place is treated as a selected event or calendar state, OmniView can present invented precision as the requested world.
When geography, habitation, or camera support is inferred from a label instead of the dated site, the prompt can invent land, universal absence, or an impossible witness position.
When a visual verb, failed dispatch, comparison, or traversal is interpreted as broader authority than supplied, the host can incur unapproved external calls or report a render that never returned.
When harness route, model identity, execution, or evidence boundaries are overstated, a private handoff can be trusted for behavior it never observed.
When portable files diverge, references escape, manifests drift, or private development paths enter the package, one host can receive broken or sensitive bytes.
When kit inventory, checksums, ZIP topology, local links, or repeated builds diverge, the recipient cannot establish what was delivered or safely open it.

When prerequisites, result states, stop conditions, recovery, or evidence limits are missing, a maintainer or skill user can damage work, retry an uncertain external action, or describe an unverified state as healthy.
When grounding source-card structure or internal visible-claim links break, behavioral prompts can consume an incoherent evidence corpus.
When private-preview language or GL4SS attribution is incomplete, a recipient can infer public redistribution rights or official upstream status that do not exist.
When the known unknown-habitation fallback is presented as repaired, the maintainer receives a broader patch claim than the code earns.
